query: I need a slide deck for a 10-minute update to my engineering team summarising the three research notes in ./sources. Make it something I can present from and share as a PDF afterwards.
expected_behavior: Reads all three source notes in full before drafting
Produces a presentable deck and a PDF, both inside the working directory
Fits roughly 10 minutes, with speaker notes on every slide
Keeps the sources' claims and caveats intact: open decisions stay open, untested results are labelled untested
Renders the slides to images and fixes overflow or clipping before finishing

query: Make me a short slide deck explaining how a web request flows through our system: browser, CDN, load balancer, API service, a job queue, background workers, and Postgres. Include what happens when a worker fails. It should be diagram-heavy; the audience are new engineers in their first week.
expected_behavior: Most content slides carry a diagram rather than bullets
Shows all seven components, the synchronous versus queued paths, and the worker-failure path (retry, backoff, dead-letter)
Diagram text stays legible at slide size and connectors do not cross labels
States which architecture details are assumptions for the user to verify
Keeps the diagram source editable without hand-placing coordinates

query: I'm giving a 5-minute lightning talk at a local developer meetup called 'Why boring technology wins'. Build the slides, with speaker notes I can read from on each slide.
expected_behavior: Every slide has read-aloud speaker notes whose timings add up to about 5 minutes
Credits borrowed ideas (for example Dan McKinley's 'Choose Boring Technology')
Uses placeholders rather than guessing the speaker's name or the meetup
Has a polished, consistent look without a theme being requested

query: I'm giving a 20-minute talk to non-technical managers about adopting AI coding agents in our team. Draft the outline first and wait for my feedback before you build any slides.
follow_up: Thanks. Move the risks section before the benefits, drop the history part entirely, and add a slide about cost. Then build the deck.
expected_behavior: Turn 1 returns an outline only and builds no files
Turn 2 applies every requested change, and says so when a requested change has nothing to act on
Cost figures it does not know are placeholders, not invented numbers
The finished deck has speaker notes and fits 20 minutes with time for questions
